review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the related Unramified/Inertia/Basic.lean (`isArithFrobeniusLift_iff`, `IsArithFrobeniusLift.apply_of_pow_eq_one`) and the ExplicitCyclotomicSymbol/ArtinMap.lean block that repeats the `hτz` argument. The other repeated shapes are short: `restrictNormalHom_commutes` rewrites, `QuotientGroup.mk_surjective` lifts, and the `Units.mk0 (p : ℚ_[p]) …` term. I judged these too small for this rubric. The two restriction-to-a-finite-level arguments (Frobenius in the private lemma, trivial in the `p`-power lemma) use different final steps. I did not check that the proposed replacement lemma compiles. I did not check the coprimality `(p^f−1).Coprime p` in detail, although `Nat.coprime_pow_sub_one` is used in ArtinMap.lean. I did not check that the `SeparableClosure`/`AlgebraicClosure` transfer lemma exists in a usable form.

findings.problem: The argument that an arithmetic Frobenius lift `g` of `ℚ_[p]` sends `z` with `z ^ (p ^ f - 1) = 1` to `z ^ p` appears twice. First `z^(p^f−1)=1` becomes `z^(p^f)=z` by `Nat.sub_add_cancel`, `pow_succ` and `one_mul`. Then `isArithFrobeniusLift_iff` is applied with `Nat.card` rewritten by `simpa`. The same text is in ExplicitCyclotomicSymbol/ArtinMap.lean (`hgN`, with `hpow`). The `X^(q^f) − X` step is the nontrivial part. A neighbouring lemma, `IsArithFrobeniusLift.apply_of_pow_eq_one`, already packages the same kind of step for orders prime to the residue characteristic, so this is a third ad hoc variant.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma, e.g. in Local/Cyclotomic.lean or next to `apply_of_pow_eq_one`: `theorem IsArithFrobeniusLift.apply_of_pow_card_pow_sub_one {K} … {σ} (hσ : IsArithFrobeniusLift K σ) {f : ℕ} (hf : f ≠ 0) {z : AlgebraicClosure K} (hz : z ^ (Nat.card 𝓀[K] ^ f - 1) = 1) : σ z = z ^ Nat.card 𝓀[K]`. The proof sketch is: `z ^ q^f = z` by `Nat.sub_add_cancel` and `pow_succ`, then `isArithFrobeniusLift_iff.1`. The `ℚ_[p]` case then follows by rewriting with `Padic.natCard_residueField`. Alternatively state it directly as `p ^ f - 1`. With this, `hτz` becomes `fun z hz ↦ by simpa [Padic.natCard_residueField] using hτF.apply_of_pow_card_pow_sub_one hf (by simpa [Padic.natCard_residueField] using hz)`, and `hgN` in ArtinMap.lean (lines 159–163) becomes the same call. Both users keep their hypotheses (`hf : f ≠ 0`, `hτF`/`hgF` from `isArithFrobeniusLift_of_mk_eq_artinMap_uniformizer`).
findings.benefit: The `X^(q^f) − X` computation is stated and maintained once. The two proofs lose their inlined power rewriting. Readers of the prescription theorem see a named fact instead of a re-derivation.

findings.excerpt: absoluteGaloisGroupRestrictEquiv K σ x = x ^ Nat.card 𝓀[K] := by
findings.problem: This private lemma re-proves, inside `SeparableClosure K`, that a lift of the Artin symbol of a uniformizer sends every root of `X^{q^f} − X` to its `q`-th power. It sets up a local-field structure on the unramified extension `𝓤 f` (four `let`/`have` instances), compares Frobenius via `artinMap_restrict` and `localArtinMap_uniformizer`, then uses `restrictNormalHom_commutes`. The library already has this fact in `isArithFrobeniusLift_iff`, applied to `isArithFrobeniusLift_of_mk_eq_artinMap_uniformizer`. That pair is used in `abelianizedLocalCyclotomicCharacter_artinMap` (`hφu`) and in the prescription theorem (`hτz`). So the same Frobenius-lift statement is derived by two separate routes in one file. The only difference is `SeparableClosure` versus `AlgebraicClosure`.
findings.proposed_change: State the lemma through `IsArithFrobeniusLift`. The hypothesis `hσ` gives `IsArithFrobeniusLift K σ` by `isArithFrobeniusLift_of_mk_eq_artinMap_uniformizer K hπ σ hσ`. Then `isArithFrobeniusLift_iff.1` gives `σ y = y ^ q` for `y : AlgebraicClosure K` with `y ^ q^f = y`. Transport to `SeparableClosure K` along the existing `coe_absoluteGaloisGroupRestrictEquiv_apply` (used in Padics/MultiplicativeCompletion/Reciprocity.lean) applied to `(x : AlgebraicClosure K)`. The same transport lemma can serve `localArtinMap_cyclotomic_uniformizer`, which could use `IsArithFrobeniusLift.apply_of_pow_eq_one` for the root of unity in the algebraic closure. The unramified-extension instance block and `hres` then disappear.
findings.benefit: There would be one derivation of 'Frobenius lift acts by `q`-th power on roots of `X^{q^f}−X`' instead of two independent ones. The roughly 30-line private lemma, with its heavy instance setup, would become a short transport statement. The file's cyclotomic results would also share the `IsArithFrobeniusLift` API used elsewhere in the file.
